mainEntity.name: What is the difference between a lean-to addition and a clear-span frame extension?

acceptedAnswer.text: A lean-to addition attaches to the sidewall or endwall of an existing building with a single-slope roof, making it a cost-effective choice for covered equipment storage, workshops, or small office space. A full clear-span frame extension continues the existing building's structural profile, maintaining interior ceiling clearance without central support posts. While a lean-to involves less steel and simpler engineering, it limits interior height and width compared to a clear-span addition, which creates an unobstructed open floor plan suitable for heavy equipment or large-scale commercial operations.
acceptedAnswer.description: A lean-to is a single-slope attachment ideal for smaller storage, while a clear-span extension continues the building's main profile for open, unobstructed square footage.
